questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 ?
questions.explain: Count the 4s: there are 5 of them, so this is 5 groups of 4, which is 5 × 4 = 20. Counting one group too many gives 6 × 4, which is 4 too much, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 4 × 4 or 6 × 5. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stemText: Wei Jie works out 3393 + 3235 in columns. One column makes 12, so he writes 2 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 12 is the tens column: 9 + 3 = 12, and no other column reaches ten. 12 tens is 1 hundred and 2 tens, so the 2 stays in the tens column - worth 20 - and the small 1 goes above the hundreds column - worth 100. The small 1 is worth 100. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.explain: Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one in each column ignores which number is on top, and that is how 4305 appears. questions.stemText: Which of these fractions is between 1/6 and 6/12?
questions.explain: Step 1: the two ends are not written in the same size of piece, so cut 16 into 12ths first: 1 × 2 = 2 and 6 × 2 = 12, so 16 is the same amount as 212. Step 2: now every fraction is in 12ths, so just count the tops - the answer has to be more than 2 of them and fewer than 6. That is 312. 16 and 612 are the two ends themselves, so neither of them is between them.

questions.stem: Nurul works out 4.54 + 5.8. Nurul writes the 8 underneath the 4 and gets 5.12. What is the correct answer?
questions.stemText: Nurul works out 4.54 + 5.8 . Nurul writes the 8 underneath the 4 and gets 5.12 . What is the correct answer?
questions.explain: Line up the decimal POINTS, not the last digits. Write 4.54 and 5.8 one under the other with the points in a column, filling the short one out with a zero: 4.54 + 5.80 = 10.34. Writing the 8 under the 4 slides 5.8 one whole column to the right, and that is where 5.12 comes from.

questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 15 cm long and 9 cm wide. A notch 6 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 6 cm of edge before the notch and 3 cm after it, and the banner is still 7 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 6 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 3 + 9 + 15 + 9 = 52 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 6 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 6 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (15 + 9) + 2 × 2 = 52 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
